message.reasoning:
I'm checking the orbital period next, working from a semi-major axis of 6978 km and Earth's gravitational parameter, and I've started cubing the axis.

Checking the period came out to about 5,801 seconds, roughly 97 minutes, which works out to around 14.9 orbits per day. The sun-synchronous inclination at 600 km and the precession rate both look right, and the ground-track shift per orbit comes to roughly 2,700 km. The 60 km swath and the five neighbouring passes to cover the reef also check out.

I'm now weighing whether a single pass can cover the whole reef, since the track spacing at its latitude is larger than the reef's length and each day only gives one pass over any given stretch.

I'm working through whether the ground track runs roughly north-south along the reef, so that a single pass could cover its full length within one orbit.

I'm checking how the swath and the reef's width interact with the spacing between passes. The 2,700 km gap between neighbouring tracks at the equator means passes on the same day are too far apart to cover the reef's width, so the five passes would have to fall on different days.

I'm weighing whether five neighbouring passes can actually cover the reef's width, since the tracks are 2,700 km apart and wouldn't line up as adjacent strips. That points toward off-nadir pointing or a repeat cycle that shifts the tracks gradually, which takes several days.

I'm checking whether the reef's latitude changes the ground-track spacing, since it sits well south of the equator and the shift per orbit shrinks with cosine of latitude. I'm also confirming the 97.8° sun-synchronous inclination for 600 km, and I'm starting to work out the ground sample distance from altitude and detector pixel size.

Now I'm weighing whether the 10 m resolution is fine enough for colour-change work at reef scale, since the cited airborne method uses about 1 m imagery. I'm also noting that the 100 m bathymetry claim is shaky, and that the mission's "detected within days" aim doesn't quite match a weekly revisit.

I'm checking the claim about 30 percent more acidity, which corresponds to a pH drop of about 0.1, and the bleaching losses of roughly 30 percent in 2016 and 20 percent in 2017 against their cited sources. The two bleaching figures look broadly right, and the satellite contact count over Australia is plausible, though I haven't analysed the communications stage yet.

I'm checking the reference list now: the Nature-style news piece on Hawaiian bleaching mapping is a secondary source rather than a primary one, but the quoted wording matches. The citations look numbered in order of first appearance, with the project plan citing [7], [8], [4] and [5] again.

I'm checking the reference formatting now: the numbering runs in order of first appearance, and most entries look fine. A few sources, such as the ResearchGate link and the NOAA Coral Reef Watch report, lack authors or dates, so I'm noting those as weaker citations.

I'm checking the mission's requirements against the document now: the space segment covers the course material on launch and orbits, but launch is only mentioned in the Gantt chart, so that requirement is only partly met. Software selection (STK) meets its requirement, and the Gantt chart and its stage colouring match the text.

I'm checking the mission timeline against the Gantt chart: End of Life and ground control both line up with the text, and the final design runs through week 9 as stated. The one mismatch I'm noting is that the text says week 10 is float with no new design work, yet the Gantt still shows STK simulations running into that week.

I'm now checking the plan for a timing conflict: the Gantt chart runs STK simulations into Week 10, and the editing section calls that week the place for final simulations, yet the text says final design and simulation should finish by the end of Week 9.

I'm checking the Gantt chart's date labels against the report's September to November 2020 timeframe and the 20 November deadline, which falls on the Friday of Week 10, so those line up. I'm also noting that the report's table of contingencies starts a line about relaxing the first objective to fortnightly coverage, which I haven't read in full yet.

Now I'm weighing whether the progress so far counts as evidence of an STK scenario, since the calculations are there but no simulation output has been shown yet.

I'm checking whether the swath-based argument actually holds: the five-pass reasoning isn't tied to a computed revisit time, and I'd need the repeat cycle to say whether weekly coverage is achievable.

I'm checking the reef-length point against the north-south orientation, and the 10 m ground sample distance seems adequate for reef-scale features. I'm also weighing whether the visible-band colour and tone changes are enough to follow the method the sources describe.

I'm looking at the mission concept's user list (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO and universities, BoM) and checking that the objectives tie back to those needs. The goal and objectives are stated clearly, though some are still marked "to be refined." I'm also noting a few weaker references, such as the ResearchGate and WWF sources, and a depth-mapping claim that doesn't seem directly relevant.

I'm now looking at how the mission concept ties to satellite monitoring versus the existing NOAA Coral Reef Watch products, which already use sea-surface temperature data. On the project plan, the Gantt chart, risks table and rationale for ordering all link back to the mission, though the week 10 timing conflict pulls its robustness down a little.

I'm noting that the figure caption and table labels are fine, but several references lack dates or authors, and the Gantt chart's red deadline lines aren't actually visible. I'm also flagging an awkward sentence in the introduction, and a causal claim that overstates acidification as the main driver of bleaching, when warming is the usual cause.

I'm noticing that the claim about acidification driving bleaching is technically off, since heat stress is the usual cause, and the "displacing billions of animals" wording has no support I can see. I'm also weighing the background paragraph's mention of fossil fuels and deforestation, which seems fine, and the traditional plane-based surveying line, which also reads correctly.

I'm going through the reference formatting and the page length now, though I can't confirm the page count from what's here. The software choice is fine, since STK is the tool the brief allows. I'm settling on a level for the presentation criterion, leaning between Accomplished and Adequate, because the writing is solid but the reference gaps and awkward sentences hold it back.

I'm settling on a level for the presentation criterion around 8, since the writing and figures are clear and the references are mostly in order. I'm also noting that the criterion weighting and the level scales don't line up, so the mark needs to stay within whichever level descriptor fits.

I'm weighing how the level ranges map onto the criterion weights, since the descriptors top out at 10 while the criterion is worth 40. Scaling an 8 out of 10 up to the 40-point weight would give 32, so I'll keep the mark inside the level range and check how the scale converts.

I'm settling the marks on the level scale, so each figure has to sit inside the range of the level I've chosen. For the mission concept, I'm giving it a 9 as Accomplished, since the goal and users are clear even though a few references are weak.

I'm settling the remaining marks on the level scale, and for the mission concept I'm keeping the score at 8 because the objectives are still partly unvalidated and one causal claim overstates acidification's role. The project plan and the analysis also come out at 8, and the presentation at 8, since the writing is clear but the references and a few sentences hold it back.

Now I'm going through the requirement checks and the technical issues. The mission concept's acidification claim looks wrong, since bleaching is driven mainly by thermal stress, and the "billions of animals" figure has no support I can see. The coverage argument in the progress section also seems incomplete, because the revisit time was never worked out from a repeat cycle.

I'm now listing the remaining issues: the Week 10 timing clash between the plan text and the Gantt chart, and the 10 m ground sample distance, which isn't justified against the airborne method it draws on. I'm also checking the hand calculation for sun-synchronous orbit.

I'm drafting the evidence quotes now, starting with the mission concept's goal of giving reef managers repeatable observations of coral colour across the whole reef. I'm checking that each quote is an exact, contiguous passage from the document and short enough to meet the limit.

I'm checking the evidence quotes now, making sure each one is an exact passage from the mission document and short enough to meet the word limit. I'm also settling how to lead with the objectives that come from the managers' need to respond within days.

I'm drafting the evidence quotes now, checking each one against the document word for word and keeping it within the word limit. I'm also noting the acidification sentence as an overstatement, and the Week 10 wording as clashing with the Gantt chart.

I'm working out the evidence quotes for the coverage and orbit-calculation points, checking that each one matches the mission document exactly and stays within the word limit.

I'm settling on the evidence quotes now, making sure each one is copied exactly from the mission document and stays within the word limit. For the launch point, the project plan only says the launch options still need to be reviewed, so I'll quote that line as the evidence for the partial coverage of requirement 2.

I'm now settling the remaining requirement checks: the STK design work and the Gantt-based weekly structure both look covered, and the hand calculations for the candidate orbit support the coverage claim. I'm drafting the evidence quotes for these points, keeping each one an exact passage from the mission document and within the word limit.

I'm drafting the last evidence quotes now, lining up the background-reading and STK tutorial lines for the project-management criterion, along with the NOAA reference for the references check. I'm also planning to bring the Week 10 timing issue into the evidence for the coverage point.

I'm mapping the remaining requirement checks onto the document's sections, tying R2 to the preliminary progress and R3 through R5 to the project plan. I'm also drafting a short overall summary: a strong Part 1 with clear mission concept, Gantt chart, risks and verified orbit calculations, held back by the missing launch analysis, the acidification error, the unjustified ground sample distance, the Week 10 inconsistency, the incomplete coverage argument and the weak references.

Next I'm turning to the remaining technical issues, starting with the mission concept's acidification claim, which blames bleaching on ocean acidity when thermal stress is the main driver. I also want to flag the unsupported "billions of animals" figure and the 10 m ground sample distance target, which still needs justification against the method it draws on.

I'm wrapping up the technical issues list, with the last item being the Week 10 timing clash between the plan text and the Gantt chart. I'm weighing whether to add a cloud-free weekly requirement point, but I'm leaning toward keeping the list to the five issues already identified.
